title: A trouble clear carries the clearer's measured hand
intention: cairn/tools/base DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble stamps the clearer's measured caller onto the clear_trouble emission as values['hand'] = {class, unit, ancestry} from cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.caller(), read in the clearer's own process at the moment of the clear, beside the self-declared 'by'.
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. Measured 2026-10-11 by cc0 after Akien ran ~/.akien/temp/clear-who-writes-what.sh (commons 9306593): all 9 clears landed in the trouble records as cleared_by {by: 'akien'}, but (1) the commons .artifact-journal.jsonl records every one of those 9 'clear' writes with caller class 'gate', because the write happens in the trouble device's process at the drain (cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py _fold, CLEAR_GATE), not in the clearer's; so cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:164-176, which teaches a row only when the clear's journal caller class is 'akien', taught NO row: a read-only block.compile(block.read_journals()) on 2026-10-11 returns increments [] and every who-writes-what clear in the journal as disposition cleared:gate, so no clear has taught a row since the block was armed; and (2) every one stays standing OPEN, because its notified set is ['cc'] (DEFAULT_RECIPIENTS) and trouble.py clear() closes only when every notified recipient has cleared. The clearer's hand is lost at the emission: cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py clear_trouble emits {by, what_changed} and nothing measured; 'by' is a self-declared word.
traces_to: Law 3 (who cleared is measured, not declared); Law 6 (the learning that only Akien's hand may teach needs his hand measured); Law 7 (the record of a clear says whose it was).
how: cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py clear_trouble only: import caller from cairn.tools.artifact.artifact (its declared public_interface); values={'by': by, 'what_changed': what_changed, 'hand': caller()}. A caller() that raises (no /proc) stamps hand={'class': 'unknown', 'error': '<type>: <msg>'} and the clear still emits: a clear is never lost to its own measurement (Law 7, loud on the record). Docstring names this ticket and the measurement. reconcile_troubles is untouched (its clears are machine reconciles, by='<scope owner>').
falsifier: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_clear_carries_the_clearers_hand.py under PROVES {'c2172127d7a4': {'1','2'}} with emissions into a scratch log root: (1) clear_trouble(...) from the proof process writes an emission whose values.hand.class equals cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.caller()['class'] measured in the same process, and whose hand carries a non-empty ancestry; (2) with caller monkeypatched to raise OSError, the emission still lands, with hand.class 'unknown' and the error named. Hollow: dropping the hand key reds both.
watchme: none, because the fault is measured at /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/who-writes-what-cairncommons-slates-bulk-cc.json (and its 8 siblings) and is re-measured by Akien's next who-writes-what clear once 0539e85f8b2d is PROVED
intent_berth: none, because this is a bug entering as a ticket (skills/intent/SKILL.md, the TICKET entry point), born from the measured fault at /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/who-writes-what-cairncommons-slates-bulk-cc.json

decisions.text: Measure at the emission, in the clearer's process, with the same caller() the artifact journal uses: the trouble device's own process can only ever measure itself ('gate'), which is the measured fault. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
'by' stays beside 'hand': it is the clearer's word and the record keeps both; readers that judge whose hand it was read 'hand'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
